title: The initial Islet-1 blueprint
summary: The first public version of the blueprint: {{studies}} studies and {{findings}} findings, the Idea Graveyard, {{designs}} designs scored on five tests, and the five layers of checks.

title: Test delayed and reduced vascular oxygen support together
summary: Asks what happens to the graft's oxygen supply when new blood vessels connect late and carry less oxygen than hoped, both at once.

outcome.note: The blueprint now tests late-forming blood vessels and weaker oxygen delivery together, under both ways the cells release oxygen, and publishes the whole grid, so it shows where the oxygen margin runs out.

title: The published chance-of-working estimate does not compute the quantity it states, and omits failure modes the blueprint already documents
summary: Asks that the odds on the Blueprint page say exactly what they measure, how the three-design figure is worked out, and which checks they leave out.

outcome.note: The odds now define each step as a design still in the running clearing the next hurdle, give the reason for each hurdle's three-design figure, and name the lab checks that sit outside the four hurdles, so they cannot be read as the chance of a cure.

title: Measure endocrine function after the modelled oxygen bridge and during recovery
summary: Asks whether the cells that survive the 14-day low-oxygen window still release insulin and glucagon normally afterwards, and adds a side-by-side lab test during and after recovery.

outcome.note: The blueprint now tests whether the cells that survive the 14-day low-oxygen window after transplant still release insulin and glucagon normally during and after recovery, separating lost cells from weakened ones before counting the working dose.
